However, none appears on behalf of the victim/prosecutrix to contest the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellants.
Therefore, we proceed further to consider the above bail applications.

Heard Shri Dharmesh Shrivastava and Shri Arjit Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellants, and Shri Avinash Singh, learned Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (IA-1 of 2023).

Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the appellants have been falsely implicated in the case and there is no evidence on Cra 1571 and 1633 of 2023 record to connect the appellants with Satyam Sahu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150551741/

sentences.text: It is further argued by the learned counsel for the appellants that the victim/prosecutrix, a major girl at the time of incident, left her house with appellant- Satyam Sahu on her own will to meet the co-accused/ other appellant- Irfan Khan, with whom she was having love affair.
Most of the witnesses are interested witnesses and there are contradictions, omissions and improvements in their statements, which have not been scrutinized carefully by the trial Court.
Appellant-Irfan Khan and the victim/prosecutrix are known to each other from 2017, and they are having cordial/friendly relationship on her own consent on the pretext of marriage.
Medical report Ex.P15 also does not support the prosecution case.
Father of the Victim lodged the missing report of his daughter based upon which First Information Report against the accused appellants has been lodged.
Appellants were on bail during trial and they have not mis-used the liberty granted to them.
Therefore, in these circumstances, appellants may be enlarged on bail.
Learned State counsel though opposes the bail applications but does not dispute the fact of victim's cordial relationship with appellant- Irfan Khan and about the period of their knowing each other.
Appellants were on bail during trial.
Cra 1571 and 1633 of 2023
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, also considering the fact, that co-accused/appellant- Irfan Khan and the victim, both of them were having cordial/friendly relationship with each other from 2017 till 2021, Medical report (Ex.P15) of the victim in which no external injury was found by Dr Sushila Kindo (PW8), unexhibited FSL report of clothing of the victim on which insufficient stains were found, appellants were on bail during trial, and they are in jail since 03.02.2023, hearing of this appeal would take some time, without commenting anything on merit, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellants.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to the appellants by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.

They shall be released on bail on each of them executing bail bond in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for their appearance before the Registry of this Court on 2nd February, 2024.

They shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to them by Cra 1571 and 1633 of 2023 the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.

Consequently, bail applications filed on behalf of the appellants (IA-1 of 2023 in CRA-1571 of 2023 filed by appellant-Satyam Sahu and IA-1 of 2023 in CRA-1663 of 2023 filed by appellant- Irfan Khan), are allowed.
It transpires from the record that the matter is ripe for final hearing.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing after three months.
